messages:
sean: heads-up — the progressive rollout to model-v2 in eu-west-1 stalled during the traffic ramp. intended 0->30% over 10m but cluster stuck at ~5% for ~12m. noticed this at 08:04 UTC.

maya: ugh. any errors in the rollout-controller logs?

sean: rollout-controller shows repeated `batcher timeout` and a couple of `failed to patch service` entries. no gitops errors. deploy-bot says the k8s manifests were reconciled by argocd at 08:03 with no diff.

deploy-bot: started rollout model-v2 -> target 30% traffic (annotation: rollout.strategy=progressive, rollout.window=10m)

alex: can you paste the controller snippet? also check the service targetPort/selector — sometimes traffic doesn't split if the service selector is slightly different from the new pods.

sean: snippet attached (copied):
```
E083 08:04:15.123 controller.go:342] batcher timeout waiting for endpoints consistency
W083 08:04:16.591 controller.go:411] failed to patch Service/model-service: timed out waiting for adm server
I083 08:04:20.003 autoscaler.go:88] requested pool scale (gpu-pool-eu) to +2 but AWS ASG cooldown prevents new instances until 08:10
```

liam: oh — autoscaler cooldown + ASG cap hit. That would explain why the new pods stayed Pending and endpoints didn't update. Did Terraform recently change the ASG max?

maya: I checked infra PRs — there was a stealth bump to `max_size = 12` last week but the pool was already at 12 and some instances are reserved by infra-testing. so ASG refused to scale.

sean: interestingly the automated rollback didn't trigger either. our alerting metric is `p95-latency` on the canary route, which stayed fine (requests routed to the stable replica because traffic never fully switched) — rollout-controller relies on `rollout.redwood/fallback: enabled` annotation to auto-revert when endpoints fail. looks like that annotation wasn't present in the argocd-managed manifest (we rely on a kustomize overlay to inject it).

alex: so two failure modes: infra capacity blocked pod readiness -> endpoints stale -> rollout batcher times out; and control-plane config missed the `fallback` annotation so automated rollback guardrail didn't run.

liam: agreed. quick mitigation: 1) manually increase ASG cap to allow scale, or temporarily free reserved instances, 2) patch the rollout manifest to add `rollout.redwood/fallback: enabled` so future runs can auto-revert, 3) add an alert for `endpoints.count < expected` during progressive ramps.

maya: I can open a small infra PR to bump ASG max to 14 and un-reserve one instance from infra-testing, but that's 15m approval. meanwhile can we force the rollout to abort and revert?

sean: yes — performing an emergency abort via rollout-controller: `kubectl -n models rollout abort model-service/model-v2-rollout` will flip traffic back to stable. doing that now.

sean: done. traffic back to 100% stable. no user impact reported. marking incident as P2 and will follow-up with a postmortem.

deploy-bot: rollout model-v2-rollout aborted by sean at 08:18 UTC. Reverted to stable.

alex: follow-ups: (a) make `rollout.redwood/fallback` injected by default in argocd overlays, (b) add a pre-check in the progressive-rollout job that validates pool capacity (ASG desired + needed > max -> fail-fast), (c) improve rollout-controller error message for `batcher timeout` so it surfaces capacity vs network patch failures.

maya: I'll file the infra PR + link a short runbook for on-call to check ASG/instance reservations during ramps.

liam: and I'll add a small k8s probe to detect `endpoints.count` drift and fire an alert that triggers an automated rollback if traffic didn't increase after X minutes.

sean: cool. thanks team. can we also add a short note to the rollout docs about the dependency chain: autoscaler -> node provisioning -> pod readiness -> endpoints -> traffic split? saved me some head-scratching. :+1:

maya: yes — will add that to the docs and include the kustomize overlay requirement.

alex: great. tying this into the postmortem template. we should include a timeline and the missing annotation root cause.

sean: ping me when infra PR is merged and argocd has the overlay change — we'll re-run the progressive rollout on a small test model.

liam: noted. adding owners and TODOs to the incident thread.

sean: thanks. closing this slack thread for now.
